findings.finding: Active attempts to recall information are more effective for learning than passive repetition.
findings.quote: Active repetition is very much more effective than passive repetition. ... there are two ways of introducing further repetitions. We may re-read this list: this is passive repetition.

findings.finding: Effortful retrieval processes lead to better long-term memory than easier, passive methods.
findings.quote: difficult but successful retrievals are better for memory than easier successful retrievals

findings.finding: Retrieval practice helps identify errors and misconceptions while improving long-term retention.
findings.quote: Using retrieval practices also produces less forgetting than studying and restudying while helping to identify misconceptions and errors with effects lasting years.

principle: Actively recalling information from memory is more effective for long-term retention than passively reviewing or repeating material.
for_the_teacher: Ask the learner to perform a dance phrase from memory before showing them the video again.
Encourage the learner to attempt a difficult step without visual aids before providing a demonstration.
Incorporate 'test' moments where the learner must recall the sequence of steps without the teacher's guidance.
Provide feedback only after the learner has made an active attempt to recall and execute the movement.
